reviews.complexity: O(n log n+k log k) time, O(n+k) space

reviews.solution_rationale: After sorting, the first sum is the m smallest values. Best-first generation must enumerate increasing m-index combinations using nonnegative replacement costs without O(m) work or duplicate generation per result. A persistent heap or canonical partition-state enumeration is needed; Specialist uncertainty: I have not established its full transitions and bound.
reviews.complexity: O((n+k) log(n+k)) intended enumeration; successor representation uncertain

reviews.solution_rationale: Process tree edges in decreasing speed with DSU. Joining components of sizes A and B contributes speed*A*B because that edge is the bottleneck for all newly connected pairs.
reviews.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Multi-source BFS gives distance to the nearest coin at every vertex. The answer is dist(a,b)+2*minimum nearest-coin distance on path(a,b), queried with binary-lifting path minima and LCA.
reviews.complexity: O((n+q) log n) time, O(n log n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Merge-sort the indices using interactive comparisons, which needs fewer than 10^4 comparisons for n<=1000. Assign sorted ranks back to indices and flush each query.
reviews.complexity: O(n log n) queries and time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Prune coinless leaves to form the fixed coin Steiner subtree. For each query compute the edge count of its union with a and b via nearest core projections and LCA distances; the shortest covering walk costs twice that edge count minus dist(a,b).
reviews.complexity: O((n+q) log n) time, O(n log n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Charge each distinct value in a subarray to its first occurrence. Position i contributes (i-previousOccurrence)*(n-i+1), which sums all distinct counts without enumerating subarrays.
reviews.complexity: O(n) expected time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Stable-sort value/index pairs. A value moves left at most one position per bubble round, and the maximum original-index minus sorted-index displacement equals the number of required rounds (zero if already sorted).
reviews.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: After k left-to-right bubble passes, output is generated by a min-heap initially containing the first k+1 elements: repeatedly pop the minimum and insert the next input, then drain. Each element can migrate left by at most k while large elements propagate right.
reviews.complexity: O(n log(min(k,n)+1)) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Introduce a node per bus company with city-to-company edges costing its ticket and company-to-city zero-cost edges. Dijkstra on this sparse bipartite graph avoids quadratic company cliques.
reviews.complexity: O((n+m+sum k) log(n+m)) time, O(n+m+sum k) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Zero requires an equal-sum partition, found by bitset subset-sum with predecessor recovery for newly reachable sums. Maintain the two equal-sum groups, subtract one value from each and return the residual to the larger side until zero remains, producing legal operations.
reviews.complexity: O(nS/w+S) word-operation time, O(S+n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: For each divisor count input multiples, giving 2^count-1 subsets whose gcd is divisible by it. Subtract answers of proper multiples in descending order to isolate each exact gcd.
reviews.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Turn each query into two value-threshold events, sort elements and events by value, and maintain a Fenwick tree on indices to count the requested index interval.
reviews.complexity: O((n+q) log(n+q)) time, O(n+q) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Factor k. For each prime power p^e, adjacent exponents must have at least one equal to e. A two-state recurrence for full exponent versus one of e smaller exponents is powered by a 2x2 matrix; multiply independent prime contributions.
reviews.complexity: O(t sqrt(k)+sum distinct prime factors * log n) time, O(sqrt(max k)) sieve space

reviews.solution_rationale: Greedily choose the smallest unused value not consecutive to the previous one until at most six remain, then brute-force that tail in lexicographic order. On at least six unused vertices the forbidden-adjacency graph has minimum allowed degree at least N-3>=N/2, so Dirac's Hamilton-cycle theorem guarantees an extension starting at any chosen value. Handle tiny impossible inputs through the tail search.
reviews.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Track the earliest valid start of a distinct final segment using last occurrences. DP for prefix i is the sum of earlier prefix counts over allowed cuts, answered by modular prefix sums.
reviews.complexity: O(n) expected time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Factor each value and encode odd prime exponents in a bit vector over primes <=5000. Gaussian elimination over GF(2) gives rank r; the kernel has 2^(n-r) subsets with square product, including empty.
reviews.complexity: O(n P^2/w) word-operation upper bound, O(P^2/w+V) space

reviews.solution_rationale: The diagonal entry for row r xors a_i for i submasks of r by binomial parity. Pad to a power of two and perform the subset zeta transform using xor instead of addition.
reviews.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Applying 2^b pyramid reductions replaces each value by its xor with the value 2^b positions later. Apply these jump reductions for set bits of n-k and output the surviving k values.
reviews.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Gaussian elimination on integer xor vectors gives binary linear-basis rank r. The distinct subset xors form its span of size 2^r.
reviews.complexity: O(nB) time, O(B) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Run Dijkstra on container-content pairs with six legal operations weighted by actual transferred water. Record parents and stop at the cheapest state with A=x; reachable states have at least one container empty or full.
reviews.complexity: O(ab log(ab)) time, O(ab) space; only boundary states are reachable

reviews.solution_rationale: The jug reachability criterion is x<=a and gcd(a,b) divides x, from invariant divisibility and the Euclidean pouring construction.
reviews.complexity: O(n log(min(a,b))) time, O(1) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Fold k modulo 2(n-1) and 2(m-1) for coordinates. Count positive multiples of each side length through k and subtract common multiples of their lcm so corner bounces count once.
reviews.complexity: O(t log(min(n,m))) time, O(1) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Let A=n-1,B=m-1,g=gcd(A,B),L=lcm(A,B). The return period is 2L; the second half retraces the first. Interior self-crossings in the first half number ((A/g-1)*(B/g-1))/2, so distinct cells equal L+1 minus this count.
reviews.complexity: O(t log(min(n,m))) time, O(1) space

reviews.solution_rationale: BFS the board from the top-left corner using the eight knight displacements and output all distances.
reviews.complexity: O(n^2) time and space

reviews.solution_rationale: Translate to nonnegative displacements and order dx>=dy. Take max(ceil(dx/2),ceil((dx+dy)/3)) and raise it to match parity dx+dy. Exceptions are (1,0)->3, (1,1)->4 and (2,2)->4; (1,1) specifically reflects the nonnegative-quadrant boundary. A constructive attainability proof of the large-displacement bounds is the main prerequisite.
reviews.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Only values 0..k can be the mex. Maintain their window frequencies and an ordered set of absent values, reporting its minimum after each slide.
reviews.complexity: O(n log k) time, O(k) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Generate values and maintain an increasing deque of candidate minima, removing expired indices and dominated values. Xor each full-window minimum.
reviews.complexity: O(n) time, O(k) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Maintain a frequency map and distinct count, updating zero-to-one and one-to-zero transitions as values enter and leave the fixed window.
reviews.complexity: O(n) expected time, O(k) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Compress values and use Fenwick frequencies. Removing the leftmost subtracts its smaller followers; adding the new rightmost adds larger prior values, with strict inequalities for duplicates.
reviews.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Invert the suffix-array permutation and give the first suffix letter a. In suffix order, increase the letter exactly when the rank of the following suffix decreases; use the empty suffix as minimum and reject more than 26 letters.
reviews.complexity: O(n) time and space

reviews.solution_rationale: Segment-tree range queries merge sum, best prefix, best suffix and best subarray in left-to-right order, with empty sums allowed.
reviews.complexity: O(n+q log n) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Query the binary bit planes of original indices (using zero-based labels). Each returned position reveals the bits of its source index, recovering the permutation in ceil(log2 n)<=10 questions.
reviews.complexity: O(n log n) communication/time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Tournament SCCs are totally ordered. First derive strongly connected tournament counts by subtracting choices of a proper source SCC from all 2^C(n,2) tournaments. Then DP by total vertices and number of SCCs, choosing the labeled first SCC and multiplying by the remaining count.
reviews.complexity: O(n^3) time, O(n^2) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Frequency-count prefix xors and XOR-convolve the frequency vector with itself using Walsh-Hadamard transform. Positive coefficients indicate pair xors; for zero subtract the n+1 self-pairs so only nonempty subarrays qualify.
reviews.complexity: O(B 2^B+n) time, O(2^B) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Treat each constraint as an edge enforcing prefix[r]-prefix[l-1]=s. DFS assigns potentials in every component and rejects inconsistent cycles; adjacent prefix differences yield an array within the stated loose magnitude bound.
reviews.complexity: O(n+m) time and space

reviews.solution_rationale: View each prefix sum as a point (i,S_i); best ending average is the maximum slope from a previous point to the current one. Maintain the lower convex hull and binary-search its tangent, breaking equal slopes toward the earliest start.
reviews.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Subtract target a from every element; a nonempty subset has the desired average iff its transformed sum is zero. Offset subset-sum counting DP over the bounded negative-to-positive range and subtract empty.
reviews.complexity: O(n^2 V) time, O(nV) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Multi-source BFS propagates the two closest distinct shop origins per vertex. A shop city uses the best origin other than itself, while a nonshop uses its closest; keep at most two labels per vertex.
reviews.complexity: O(n+m) time and space

reviews.solution_rationale: Binary-search a partition taking i Finnish and k-i Swedish scores. Query boundary values until each chosen side dominates the other's next item; the smaller selected boundary is the kth highest, within 100 questions.
reviews.complexity: O(log n) queries and time, O(log n) cached space

reviews.solution_rationale: Perform four sign-reflected coordinate sweeps. In each quadrant a Fenwick maximum of reserved x+y over y prefixes gives a nearest Manhattan candidate; take each free site's minimum and then the maximum over free sites.
reviews.complexity: O((n+m) log(n+m)) time, O(n+m) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Four directional sweeps cover relative quadrants; sort by signed x and query a compressed-y Fenwick maximum of signed x+y for reserved points. Minimize the resulting Manhattan candidates for each free site.
reviews.complexity: O((n+m) log(n+m)) time, O(n+m) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Precompute which vertex masks are independent and subset-DP the minimum number of independent color classes covering each mask. Store chosen classes to reconstruct colors; n<=16 supports the exponential algorithm.
reviews.complexity: O(3^n) time, O(2^n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Every cell has exactly two allowed new letters, making it a Boolean variable. For every adjacent pair forbid equal-letter choice combinations with 2-SAT clauses; SCC satisfiability and assignment produce the grid or impossibility.
reviews.complexity: O(nm) time and space

reviews.solution_rationale: For each target enumerate all two-square sums up to n and remember one pair per sum. Enumerate another pair and look up n-c^2-d^2; there are O(n) pairs and total n is bounded by 10^7.
reviews.complexity: O(sum n) time, O(max n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Maintain ordered occurrence sets per value and each index's previous equal occurrence. Point updates affect only neighboring occurrences; a segment tree of previous-index maxima says [a,b] is distinct exactly when its maximum is below a.
reviews.complexity: O((n+q) log n) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: BFS from each start in the doubled vertex/parity graph. A query is possible iff the shortest walk to b of parity x mod 2 has length <=x, because any extra even length can be added by backtracking an edge.
reviews.complexity: O(n(n+m)+q) time, O(n^2+m) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Minimum vertex-disjoint path cover in a DAG equals n minus maximum matching between left/right vertex copies. Hopcroft-Karp finds the matching; accept cover size at most two and reconstruct successor chains, allowing an empty second path.
reviews.complexity: O(m sqrt n) time, O(n+m) space

reviews.solution_rationale: For each letter record whether a pair of columns has appeared together in an earlier row. A repeated pair witnesses a rectangle, after which that letter needs no more work; before success each pair is processed only once. Packed pair flags keep memory feasible.
reviews.complexity: O(kn^2+n^2) time upper bound with early stopping, O(kn^2) bits

reviews.solution_rationale: Binary-search average v and maximize prefixSumA-i*v and prefixSumB-j*v independently. Their sum being nonnegative certifies feasible prefixes; retain the maximizing indices and use enough iterations for the tolerance.
reviews.complexity: O(n log(V/epsilon)) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Use factorial-number-system blocks to unrank permutations and counts of unused smaller elements to rank them. n<=20 allows simple list deletion and signed 64-bit factorials.
reviews.complexity: O(t n^2) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: The permutation order is the lcm of cycle lengths. Factor lengths with a sieve, retain maximum prime exponents, and multiply their powers modulo the prime rather than taking gcds after modular reduction.
reviews.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Choose the n-a-b equal-card labels and count derangements on the remaining a+b labels with a excedances, then multiply by n! for first-player ordering. Derangement Eulerian DP satisfies D(r,j)=j*D(r-1,j)+(r-j)*D(r-1,j-1)+(r-1)*D(r-2,j-1), enabling precomputation.
reviews.complexity: O(N^2+t) time, O(N+t) space when queries grouped by size

reviews.solution_rationale: For an allowed final length interval [L,R], a stick of length a permits piece counts from ceil(a/R) to floor(a/L), so total piece-count feasibility can be checked through sums of these bounds. Producing all m optimal spreads requires coordinated breakpoint/heap optimization beyond separate binary searches. Specialist uncertainty: the complete efficient all-k algorithm is not established.
reviews.complexity: Near-linear/logarithmic amortized optimization intended; bound uncertain

reviews.solution_rationale: Sort values so an optimum pairs along the line. Repeatedly take the minimum adjacent-gap edge, add its cost to the next matching size, remove neighboring candidate edges, and replace the contracted edge cost by left+right-selected using a heap and linked neighbors; this encodes alternating-path exchanges.
reviews.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Standard prefix LCS DP matches equal values or drops one endpoint; backtrack through the table to output an actual common subsequence.
reviews.complexity: O(nm) time and space

reviews.solution_rationale: Map common values of the second permutation to positions in the first, then reconstruct an LIS of those positions with tail indices and predecessor links.
reviews.complexity: O((n+m) log n) time, O(n+m) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Maintain a two-stack aggregate queue, storing cumulative bitwise OR in each stack. Push generated values, pop expired values, and combine the two stack ORs for each window; this avoids a factor of word bits at n=10^7.
reviews.complexity: O(n) amortized time, O(k) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Check whether n itself is triangular, then use two pointers over triangular numbers to test a two-term representation. Gauss's three-triangular-number theorem bounds the remaining answer by three; exact integer arithmetic avoids root rounding.
reviews.complexity: O(t sqrt n) time, O(1) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Sweep Kruskal weight groups. An edge belongs to some MST iff its endpoints are in different DSU components before any edge of the same weight is merged; evaluate the whole group first.
reviews.complexity: O(m log m) time, O(n+m) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Build one MST and preprocess maximum edge weights on tree paths with LCA. Forcing edge (u,v,w) adds w and removes a maximum-weight edge on its induced cycle, so answer=MSTcost+w-pathMax.
reviews.complexity: O((n+m) log n) time, O(n log n+m) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Track extrema of x+y and x-y; their largest span equals the maximum Manhattan distance after each insertion.
reviews.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Separate x and y contributions, sort each coordinate, and sum value*i minus the preceding prefix sum. Use an accumulator wider than 64 bits if necessary for the full coordinate and point limits.
reviews.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: For each cell the largest same-letter square ending there is one plus the minimum of top, left and diagonal square sizes when their letters match. Add that size to the cell letter's count.
reviews.complexity: O(n^2) time, O(n) auxiliary space

reviews.solution_rationale: For each letter compute the largest square ending at each cell that avoids it using maximal-square DP. A square ending there contains every letter exactly when its side exceeds the maximum of those avoiding sizes; count all feasible larger sides.
reviews.complexity: O(kn^2) time, O(n^2) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Fix top and bottom rows and maintain each column's letter bitmask in that strip. A two-pointer window with a two-stack OR aggregate queue counts column intervals whose union contains all k letters in linear time per row pair.
reviews.complexity: O(n^3) amortized time, O(n) working space

reviews.solution_rationale: Precompute four directional equal-letter runs. Along each diagonal, a top-left corner remains active through min(right,down) positions; a bottom-right corner queries active starts within min(left,up) distance for its letter using Fenwick counts and expiration events.
reviews.complexity: O(n^2 log n) time, O(n^2) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Fix top/bottom rows and scan columns. Split where the two horizontal boundary letters disagree or change; within each run count pairs of columns whose entire vertical boundary has that letter. Include width-one and height-one rectangles without duplication.
reviews.complexity: O(n^3) time, O(n^2) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Maintain the maximal distinct window ending at each position using last occurrences. Its length equals the number of distinct-element subarrays ending there, so sum those lengths.
reviews.complexity: O(n) expected time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Sieve primes through 2n. For the current largest unused r choose a prime p in (r,2r], pair every i in [p-r,r] with p-i, then recurse below that interval. Bertrand's postulate guarantees the required prime and both arrays remain permutations.
reviews.complexity: O(n log log n) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Row and column totals must all be different while every symbol retains multiplicity n, so naive constant-row or Latin-square grids fail. A feasible solution requires a balanced swap construction with disjoint controlled row/column sums and special small-n handling. Specialist uncertainty: no complete construction has been established here.
reviews.complexity: O(n^2) intended constructive time; complete formula uncertain

reviews.solution_rationale: Randomly sample subset masks and hash their sums until two distinct masks collide. The total-sum bound gives at most 2^n-1 sum buckets, making birthday-scale sampling viable at n<=40. Remove common elements from the colliding subsets; positivity ensures both differences are nonempty. This is randomized expected-time reasoning, not a worst-case guarantee.
reviews.complexity: O(n 2^(n/2)) expected time, O(2^(n/2)) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Generate the array into a rolling buffer and maintain window xor by xoring out the leaving value and in the arriving value; xor all complete-window results.
reviews.complexity: O(n) time, O(k) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Convert segments to lines, sort slopes and build their upper convex envelope, discarding dominated equal slopes. Query increasing integer x with a moving hull pointer, using exact comparisons.
reviews.complexity: O(n log n+m) time, O(n) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Insert each integer-slope line only over its segment's x interval in a Li Chao segment tree. Point-query all coordinates and return -1 if no inserted segment covers the point.
reviews.complexity: O(n log^2 m+m log m) time, O(m+n log m) space

reviews.solution_rationale: Dynamic Li Chao maximum-line insertion compares lines at segment endpoints and midpoint, recursing only where the displaced line can win. Query each x along its root-to-leaf path with wide evaluation arithmetic.
reviews.complexity: O(n log X) time, O(X) space
